name: Solar Open 2
tagline: Apache-2.0 in every clause but two: name your model 'Solar', and say so in public
description: Upstage's sovereign-AI flagship: a 250B-total / 15B-active hybrid-attention MoE trained on ~12T tokens on NVIDIA B200s, with 1M-token context and an agentic-use focus. Korea's biggest open-weights swing to date, positioned to run on as little as two GPUs quantized, with NVFP4 and community GGUF builds circulating.
why: It's been on our watch list since July as a 'custom Solar License' curiosity, and the traction — 748 HF likes, ~29k downloads a month — says it's time to read the license. The read is instructive: an Apache-2.0 chassis granting perpetual, royalty-free, commercial-inclusive rights with no MAU caps and no AUP, then two bespoke conditions bolted on — derivative models must be named with a 'Solar' prefix, and public-facing materials must prominently display 'Built with Solar'.
useCases: Self-hosted agentic workloads at frontier-adjacent scale on modest GPU counts
Korean-language and sovereign-deployment scenarios where provenance matters
A case study in branding-locked licensing on an otherwise permissive base
audience: Enterprise self-hosters, sovereign-AI watchers — and anyone naming a fine-tune

setup.requirements: Multi-GPU node for full precision; Upstage claims two-GPU serving quantized, with NVFP4 and community GGUF builds available

license.notes: LICENSE file read directly on 2026-08-17. The grant is Apache-2.0-derived and broad: perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, commercial use included, no user thresholds, no acceptable-use policy, no output restrictions, standard patent-litigation termination. But two mandatory conditions attach to derivatives: the model name must begin with 'Solar', and associated websites, UIs, or documentation must prominently display 'Built with Solar'. Naming-and-promotion obligations on derived works are exactly the branding lock our methodology flags — they burden downstream identity in a way no OSI-approved license does, and the license is not OSI-approved. Kimi K3 precedent (bespoke rider on a permissive base): partial.

tally.stars: 748 HF likes, ~29.3k downloads/mo; NVFP4 and GGUF community builds active

limitations: The branding conditions propagate to every derivative regardless of scale, the bespoke license means legal review no standard text would need, and the two-GPU serving claim is Upstage's own quantized best case — plan for more.
take: The friendliest fine print we've read all summer — right up until it names your model for you. Two clauses are all it takes to leave the OSD behind.
